note: PRE-REGISTERED before any s04-s10 run. s10 locks the sha256 of this file at its first result ($V41_WORK/s10/prereg_lock.json) and refuses to run if it changes afterwards. Editing it is allowed only while no result exists. Metrics: kl32 = mean over scored tokens of sum over the teacher's top-32 of p_t (log p_t - log p_s) (GLM topk_KL); top1 = student argmax == teacher argmax; dnll = student NLL - teacher NLL; all against the cached s03 teacher, intervals = 95% row-cluster bootstrap, top-1 pairs = McNemar.

control.why: the all-384-experts replay must reproduce the cached teacher, else the replay machinery (not the masks) is being measured

arbitration.tie_rule: lowest mean kl32 wins; the winner-vs-runner-up paired difference is reported, not required to be significant

heal.adopt_if: healed - unhealed paired d_kl32 upper CI < 0 AND McNemar top-1 z > -1.96; otherwise every gain is 1.0 (unhealed)

pruned_floor.why: sanity floors for a 50% prune; GLM REAP50 v2 measured top1 0.842 / kl32 0.650, the GLM ballast failure was bucket top1 0.579, LibertAI's vision cliff was caption ppl +27.4%

multilingual.amended: 2026-10-22, owner decision, before any s10 result
multilingual.why: At 192/384 experts every selection lost multilingual on screen (round 1 winner hope_sum_pf0 0.523, random anchors 0.56-0.57). Round 2 protected the top-k multilingual experts per layer: only k=144 reached 0.657, at the cost of general/finance/science (0.792/0.771/0.764 -> 0.703/0.710/0.708), and it did not beat random significantly on kl32. The owner chose to ship hope_sum_pf0 with multilingual as a documented weakness. This bucket keeps a collapse guard (0.40) instead of min_bucket_top1; every other floor is unchanged and the cards state the limitation with the measured number.

pruned_floor.long_bins_note: Amended 2026-10-21 before any s10 result: the CONFIRM split has no row past 8k (the only held-out longctx row, 58,789 tokens, falls in SCREEN), so the long-bin clause cannot be evaluated on the release panel. It is NOT a release gate; long-context retention is reported from the SCREEN longctx row as a diagnostic and the cards say so. gates.py fails closed if long_bins_required is true and no long bin is sampled.

must_beat_random_amended.why: Owner decision AFTER the first s10 final result (confirm split). As registered, mxfp4_A vs random0 paired d_kl32 was -0.1014 [-0.2196, +0.0400]: not significant, entirely because of the multilingual bucket (kl32 1.534 vs random 0.894), the weakness the owner had already accepted on 2026-10-22 with a lowered top-1 floor. In every other bucket the keep-set has roughly half of random's kl32. The as-registered comparison stays in results.json and on the cards beside the amended one; no other threshold changes (thorA top-1 0.78 floor still applies).

nvfp4.why: lossless repack of the MXFP4 master plus the folded heal gain: it is the healed MXFP4 arm

thor_quant.why: the incremental cost of the one requantization over the same keep-set in MXFP4

waived_min_top1.why: Owner decision after the s10 final result. thorA top-1 0.7756 [0.7179, 0.8283] misses the 0.78 sanity floor (borrowed from GLM REAP50 v2's 0.842) by 0.0044, well inside its interval. It is the only 192-expert build that fits Thor; the bit-exact 128-expert alternative is far worse (top-1 0.7092, paired kl32 +0.283 vs thorA). Requantization costs kl32 +0.079 vs the MXFP4 master (limit 0.25) and top-1 -0.022. Every other clause still applies.

overlay.why: NVFP4 dense overlay is a speed lever; GLM accepted +1.56% ppl / 0.138% confident flips

trellis.why: pre-registered sub-arm of A (added 2026-10-19, before any s10 result): the same keep-set and heal with experts in KT2/KT3 bitshift-trellis blocks (ops/lib/kt.py) instead of ggml K-quants, at expert bytes <= the K-quant build's. Synthetic rows predict ~0.5x the K-quant mix's relative MSE at 2.833 bpw (ops/tests/test_kt.py); this panel is the only evidence that counts. The trellis decode costs more ALU per weight, so speed is part of the rule.
trellis.adopt_if: KT - KQ paired d_kl32 95% CI upper < max_d_kl32_hi AND McNemar top-1 z > min_top1_z AND KT expert bytes <= KQ expert bytes AND the KT build's modelled routed-expert GEMV time per token (s08 gemv_bench, M=1, summed over every layer's two passes with its allocated formats) <= max_gemv_time_ratio x the KQ build's; a missing bench means not adopted
trellis.then: if adopted, the KT build replaces thorA: the thor_quant gate (vs the shipped MXFP4/NVFP4 arm) and the A/B arm decision are re-run on this panel with thorA_kt as arm A; otherwise the K-quant build ships unchanged

arm_decision.why: pre-registered A/B at matched resident expert bytes: A = 192 experts requantized (Thor build), B = 128 experts bit-exact MXFP4
arm_decision.rule: lower mean paired kl32 wins when the paired 95% CI excludes 0; otherwise the arm with more McNemar top-1 agreement (z sign); if z == 0, B (bit-exact, proven hardware FP4 GEMV)
arm_decision.note: the '14x pruning vs quant' figure is regime-dependent and is NOT used to pre-judge this decision

gguf.why: the llama.cpp GGUF ladder (s09) of the published REAP master, scored by v41-teacher-kld against the cached source teacher on the confirm split; a level ships only if it passes
gguf.note: levels too large for full GPU offload are scored with partial -ngl from NVMe; the card states the offload

dspark_gguf.why: the checkpoint's own DSpark drafter (mtp.0-2) as an opt-in llama.cpp sidecar (dspark-*.gguf at the GGUF repo root, loaded only with --spec-type draft-dspark). Registered 2026-10-22, owner decision, before any s10 result
dspark_gguf.source_check: every tensor of our conversion equals the reference drafter GGUF (unsloth/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-GGUF dspark Q8_0): MXFP4/F32/BF16 byte-identical, Q8_0 byte-identical or dequantized relative RMSE <= source_q8_max_rel_rmse; target_layers and block_size equal
dspark_gguf.level: the largest passing GGUF level whose files + the drafter + reserve_gib fit MemAvailable after reclaim (L2, else L3); none fits -> not benched, nothing published. The card states which level the drafter fits beside
dspark_gguf.identity: greedy (temperature 0) output with the drafter vs without, same server build and level
dspark_gguf.speed: measured and reported (tok/s with and without, acceptance), not gated: the sidecar is opt-in and other hardware may gain where Thor does not
dspark_gguf.ship_rule: source_check AND identity AND acceptance pass -> upload the sidecar and state the measured numbers in the GGUF card; otherwise publish nothing and record why

s11.why: the checkpoint's own speculative head (mtp.0-2, DSpark) refit to the served REAP: always fine-tuned; base, native head and tuned head measured; in-model (pruned+K-quantized experts) preferred, separate (source MXFP4 experts) fallback
s11.identity: greedy ids with speculation == greedy ids without, at every context
s11.ship_rule: fits AND identical AND speedup > min_speedup at every context; prefer the passing in-model head, else the passing separate head, by geometric-mean speedup; none passes -> publish nothing, record in the cards
s11.inmodel_prune: s04's winning criterion on a drafter saliency bank over train anchors, the backbone's keep ratio, uniform across the 3 blocks

fit.note: resident = Thor build without mtp files + head + head window KV + main 1M-context state + workspace

traces.targets: the served REAP's greedy continuations of corpus prompts (calib split train, screen split eval); never Claude-written text

train.frozen: routed experts, embed, head, router biases
